description: ENGLISH query -> NON-ENGLISH document known-item retrieval set. Built 2026-07-24. This is the usage pattern the corpus actually sees (queries arrive in English; the corpus is mixed-language) and it had no coverage before this file: non-english-smoke.json tests non-English query -> non-English doc, which is a different thing. This is a KNOWN-ITEM set, not a relevance-labelled golden set: each query has a document it is meant to retrieve, and there is no labelling of which other documents are also relevant. Precision is therefore meaningless here; read rank and presence only.
usage: npx tsx evaluation/run-cross-lingual-eval.ts [--lanes|--full] [--label <name>] (search-service must be running)

en-tr.role: REGRESSION GUARD ONLY — not a signal class.
en-tr.construction: The non-english-smoke.json queries translated to English, targets otherwise unchanged.
en-tr.why_not_a_signal_class: These are translated TITLES. The English-bridge experiment indexes documents.title_en, and a translated native title is approximately title_en by construction ('indice de desigualdad urbana' -> 'urban inequality index' vs title_en 'Urban Inequality Index - UII'). Any bridge improvement measured here is circular. Compounding it, the zh subset is circular even WITHOUT the bridge, because zh docs already carry English catalog titles and English slugs that the metadata header puts into every chunk (e.g. nq-zh-01 translates into 'Zhuzhou Complete Street Design Manual', which is both). And the native-language baseline is already 16/16 rank-1, so the achievable delta is bounded at zero improvement. Use these to detect REGRESSION, never to claim a win.
excluded_from_smoke: nq-pt-02 dropped: its sole target 2021_medindo-mp25-com-sensores-de-baixo-custo_6821 is language='en' on qa (verified 2026-07-24). It is an English-edition PDF with a Portuguese title — the same class as the 3778/5852/2130 caveat the smoke set already records. It was authored 2026-06-11 in the pypdf era when the extracted text still looked Portuguese. On qa it is an English->English test.
nq-es-01 target 2021_el-costo-de-la-expansion-urbana-en-mexico_2705 dropped for the same reason (language='en' on qa); the query survives via its other target _9471, which is es.

en-topical.role: PROVISIONAL — filed 2026-07-24 to preserve authored work, NOT yet a validated class. The class structure is an open design question (see docs/research/2026-07-24-cross-lingual-findings.md §6).
en-topical.construction: Broad English questions of the kind a policy researcher types, where several documents are legitimately relevant and at least one is non-English. Each carries english_competitors — English documents on the same subject that will compete — because a query with no English competition is too narrow to measure anything. Relevance was verified by reading each document, not inferred from its title.
en-topical.why_it_matters: The en-body class is immune to any mechanism that indexes title or abstract text, because it was built to avoid that vocabulary. That control was designed for known-item retrieval and misapplied to mechanisms whose value is topical. For a topical query, matching an English abstract is the legitimate mechanism rather than circularity. These 12 queries are the shape that can actually show a win — and the two genuine retrieval failures found all session appeared here, not in the known-item classes.
en-topical.unvalidated: No relevance labelling beyond the target and competitor lists; no human review; authored by the same agent that formed the hypotheses.

en-body.role: THE SIGNAL CLASS. This is the only class from which a bridge result may be claimed.
en-body.construction: Authored from an actual BODY chunk of the target document, deliberately avoiding title, filename-slug and abstract vocabulary, so the query cannot be satisfied by the English handle the bridge adds. source_chunk_index and source_evidence record provenance for audit. For zh documents the source chunk was required to contain CJK characters, so the query cannot have been drawn from the English executive-summary section those documents carry (4-9% of their chunks).
en-body.coverage: The 12 non-English qa documents that the smoke set never targets. Combined with en-tr's 17, all 29 non-English searchable documents on qa are covered exactly once.

caveats: Author bias: these queries were drafted by the same agent that formed the English-bridge hypothesis. They need human review before this file is used as a gate.
Known-item retrieval is easier than real topical search. Absolute numbers here overstate health; they are useful as a BEFORE/AFTER delta, not as an absolute claim about retrieval quality.
n=27 is small. This set justifies a direction, not a threshold.
